newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers lacklustre, Med Suezmaxes steady.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers lacklustre, Med Suezmaxes steady.

text.p: The dirty tanker market was lacklustre on Thursday with rates slipping in several sectors on a general lack of enquiry, brokers said.
The Mediterranean 130,000 tonne (Suezmax) market was one of the few sectors which showed much signs of life, having picked up this week after a few weeks in the doldrums.
"There is a lot of interest. We seem to be going through a good period," said an Italian broker, referring to the Med Suezmax market which he assessed at a steady W90.
Med 80,000 tonne vessels (Aframaxes), meanwhile, were little changed at about W120 while inter-U.K./cont cargoes were also steady at W100.
Very large crude carriers (VLCCs) were steady to slightly softer with little interest seen. "Most April stems have gone and the market is waiting for May stems to come in next week," one broker said.
Mideast/west and Mideast/Singapore VLCC voyages were at W52.5/55, with Mideast/Japan at W57.5/60, down from W62.5 on Wednesday.
The Mega Pilot was one of the few Mideast VLCC fixtures, fetching W55 on a voyage to Singapore for Mitsui, loading April 25.
West Africa/U.S. and transatlantic VLCCs were quiet at W72.5 and W65 respectively.
European fuel oil edged down on low enquiry, with inter-U.K./Cont 25,000 tonne vessels slipping to W187.5 and cross-Med sliding some 15 points to W200, brokers said.

In the Caribs/upcoast sector, 70,000 tonne crude cargoes were steady to slightly firmer at W225, although Marathon was reported as fixing a vessel as high as W238, while 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil edged down to W205 from W220.
